concerns: Indonesian speakers may also use “kipas” as a context-supported shortening of “kipas angin”.
response.cue_rationale: Both answers denote a household fan that circulates air; “electric” is naturally understood for this appliance sense.

preference_risk.rationale: “Kipas” is plausibly ordinary in both varieties for a household fan, though “kipas angin” is the more explicit Indonesian form.

response.rationale: “Kipas angin” is the ordinary Indonesian term for a household electric fan, while Malaysian Malay commonly uses “kipas” for the same appliance. This is a useful national preference, not an exclusive distinction.
response.risk_rationale: The Indonesian form “kipas” may also be understood in suitable context, so the contrast is preferential rather than exclusive.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Kipas” can occur in Indonesian as a shortened contextual form, but “kipas angin” remains a credible Indonesian preference while Malaysian Malay commonly prefers “kipas.”
